description: The Alberta Official Statistic reports people working in medicine or health occupations per 1,000 population in 2011. It distinguishes large urban centres and rural/small-town areas, with Metropolitan Influence Zones defined by the share of workers commuting to an urban core. The described categories are strong 30–49%, moderate 5–29%, weak 1–4% and no commuting. Native date is May 10,2011. CSV and PDF visualisation descriptors are listed. This is an aggregate healthcare workforce-availability measure, not a count of clinics, full-time staffing or service capacity per practitioner. The Canadian Urban Data Catalogue preserves the original source identity and metadata. Source coverage is Alberta unless the described component explicitly includes Canada. The native licence field states Open Government Licence - Alberta. Access is labelled unrestricted but isopen is false; actual access and costs are unverified. No linked dataset, document, workbook, archive, installer, code or legal text was fetched. Specific simulation applications beyond the stated role are unknown.
